chapter: Band personalities, Duke's last years and the office
title: Duke's funeral
summary: Willard describes the funeral, the broadcast on WRVR and crowds along the route.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: I wasn't there that night; I had started getting ready to go to New York, because I went to the funeral in New York where Duke died.
Did Father John Sanders come down for that

funeral? Somebody told me that he spoke at Duke's funeral. I don't remember; I have a tape recording of the funeral, because the jazz station in New York, WRVR, taped it and broadcast it three times during that summer.

The radio station in New York, the jazz radio station, WRVR, and so I taped it off the radio, so I have a tape -- but I don't remember Father Sanders speaking; there were so many people. Ray Nance played, and oh, there were so many people who performed and so many people who were there. I mean, St. John's Cathedral was filled to overflowing and there were thousands of people outdoors in the streets.
Yeah, we heard it on the television and read it in the paper.
And the people were lining the streets all the way from there to the cemetery in the Bronx. It reminded me of when President Roosevelt died.
Very sad occasion. Well, he's at peace now, God rest his soul.
